maria: quick question — trying to find per-pool OOM / throttle / rate-limit events for Dedicated pools. Where do folks look for the cross-cut of pool + instance-type errors? :thinking_face:

kevin: start with Grafana -> Pools overview (left nav) then open the pool and use the 'errors & events' tab. there's a Loki link on the panel that prefilters pool=<pool_name>. also check the 'kvcache' and 'steal-queue' panels for backpressure signals. :point_right: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pools

maria: thanks — can you paste the Loki query? the dashboard filters are helpful but I want to pin a query in a ticket.

kevin: sure. copy/paste-friendly Loki snippet:
```
{job="inference-logs"} |= "OOM" |= "pool=dedicated-eu-rtx" | json | line_format "${timestamp} ${level} ${msg}"
```
for throttles (rate-limit) look for "throttle": or http_status=429 in the ingress logs:
```
{job="ingress-proxy"} |~ "429|throttle|rate limit" | json
```
Those two catch most cases.

devon: fwiw we also see two patterns: (1) kernel OOMs (killed container) which show up in node-exporter/node logs, and (2) model OOMs (runtime throws OOM) which are in inference-runtime logs. both matter.

maria: got it. for autoscale saturation signals — which specific metric do we use to indicate 'pool saturated' for alerting? cpu_util? pending_requests? kv_lag?

kevin: we've historically used a composite: pending_queue_len > 50 for 5m OR avg(active_workers/utilization) > 85% for 3m. but kv_lag is useful as early warning. here's the PromQL we use in the dashboard panel:
```
max_over_time(sum by (pool) (inference_active_workers{pool=~"$pool"}) / sum by (pool) (inference_capacity{pool=~"$pool"})[5m:])
```
if that goes > 0.85 for 3m it's a good saturation flag.

olivia: re: alerts — i've got a draft PR to split the "pool-saturation" alert into two severities (warning / critical) and to add kv_lag as a warning-level signal. i'll link the PR. :memo:

maria: perfect — ping me on the PR. also, any quick way to get traces for a specific pool when requests time out?

kevin: tracing -> service 'inference-router' -> search by tag `pool=<pool>` and time window. for timeouts we usually correlate trace id from ingress logs and jump to the trace. If you want a one-liner to grab recent slow traces for pool 'dedicated-eu-rtx':
```
service:"inference-router" tag.pool:"dedicated-eu-rtx" duration:>200ms
```
then filter for error/span status.

devon: there's also a quick k6-runbook snippet that creates a heatmap of latency per model shard — useful to tell whether it's model-side or router-side. happy to paste if helpful.

maria: yes please.

kevin: if you want i'll attach a short runbook snippet in the ticket for triage steps (check kv_lag, cpu/util, pending_queue, traces). saves time.
